Subject: On-demand export validation and redaction patterns

Rafael —

Thanks for the call yesterday. As part of our RFP we need more detail on two things for on-demand audit exports:

1) Redaction patterns: we need a short, prescriptive description of how Redwood identifies and redacts sensitive tokens (PII, PAN, SSN-like sequences) during bulk exports and an example mapping for automated redaction. Is redaction deterministic? Can we provide a regex/transform file we enforce?

2) Validation and tamper evidence: for each bulk export we require a verifiable integrity process (checksums, manifest, signed timestamps). Please describe your checksum strategy and how we provide chain-of-custody to our auditors.

Deliverables requested: sample export (schema + 3 record sample), the redaction rules file, and a short runbook describing the transfer and verification steps.

Can you confirm delivery by Friday and include any constraints on sequence length, enrichment, or streaming exports?

-James

Evergreen Bank

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: On-demand export validation and redaction patterns

James — thanks, appreciate the clear asks. 

Summary of what we'll provide by Fri (2026-07-03):
- export_spec_sample.ndjson (3-record sample, schema + metadata manifest)
- redaction_patterns_v1.xlsx (pattern list and severity tags; deterministic, configurable)
- verification_checklist.txt (step-by-step runbook for transfer + checksum verification)
- proposed SLA appendix for exports (see attached draft; final will go in contract)

Key notes now:
- Redaction: our default flow applies deterministic redaction rules that operate during the export pipeline. Patterns are expressible as regex with named capture groups. Customers can provide their own rule file (we support our spreadsheet and also JSON/NDJSON mapping). We avoid in-place irreversible transforms by default — we provide redaction tokens (e.g., <REDACTED:PII:sha256:...>) plus an optional reversible tokenization mode under dedicated contracts.

- Integrity: every export bundle includes a manifest.json with per-file sha256 and an overall signed manifest (RSA-2048) we sign with our export key. We also publish a signed ISO-8601 timestamp for when the bundle was materialized. During Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS for HMAC verification.

- Constraints: streaming exports are supported for near-real-time slices but each streamed shard emits its own manifest and sequence markers. Max single-file size is 50GB for the hosted export pipeline; we recommend chunking large harvests to 2GB files for easier verification.

Next steps: I’m looping in Karthik (engineering) to validate the sample format and Marissa (product) for SLA wording. Do you prefer S3 push or SFTP pull for the sample? We can push to a pre-signed S3 bucket or stage on a secure transfer endpoint.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes

Priya — thanks for the clarifying questions. Quick answers and what's included in the bundle: 

1) Signing key & fingerprint: attached SLA_appendix_v2.pdf includes the export signing policy. Current public key fingerprint (SHA-256): 3f:7a:9d:...:b2 (full key included in the bundle). Key rotation: quarterly; emergency rotation policy documented. Signing keys are held in Redwood HSM in hosted; for Private deployments we can bind to customer KMS.

2) Retention & deletion: deletion requests are honored immediately in the live store; archival snapshots are flagged for deletion and scheduled for secure purge. Typical archival purge window is 7–30 days depending on contract (we propose 14 days as default for Evergreen). Immutable ledger snapshots can be preserved longer under a retention clause — we will include a retention appendix with configurable windows and export flags.

3) Reversible tokenization: only available under Dedicated/Private and requires key escrow options that we document in the key management appendix. Emergency disclosure requires 2-party approval and audit logging; escrow options and SLAs documented.

Bundle contents (placed on a pre-signed S3 we will share):
- export_spec_sample.ndjson (synthetic data)
- redaction_patterns_v1.xlsx (full pattern set and examples)
- verification_checklist.txt (how to verify sha256, manifest signature, and timestamps)
- SLA_appendix_v2.pdf (draft export SLA + key management overview)

Karthik will follow up separately with a short sample manifest and a small verification script to compute and validate checksums. Rafael will send the S3 link via separate email (DocuSign/contract items notwithstanding).

Possible next step: 30-min run-through next week to walk auditors through the checklist; propose Tue 2026-07-06 10:00am PT.

Best,
Rafael
